Practice wrist flexion against a cable or band with the palm turned down, so the forearm flexors work without help from the biceps.
Stand facing a low cable pulley or an anchored band and take the handle with the palm facing down and the elbow bent. The handle sits in the palm, away from the fingertips.
Keep the elbow still and push the handle down and away by bending the wrist, letting the handle press deeper into the palm. Return slowly to the start.
Sets, repetitions, resistance, and rest follow the training plan. The video suggests two sets taken to failure, with a Exercise/Body/Strength/Farmer's Carry between sets.

The bent elbow takes the biceps out of the movement. Standard wrist curls on a bench or behind the back let the bar sink into the fingers as you tire, which strains the finger tendons and the inner elbow; this version avoids that.

Practice pulling the body toward an overhead bar through a controlled hanging range.
Day 4 at 6:42 in Person/Andrew Huberman/Book/26/Protocols/YouTube/26/09/Day 4 - Major Torso Muscles
Use an overhand grip on a secure bar and begin with the arms extended in a comfortable hanging position.
Pull the chest toward the bar by driving the elbows down and back, then lower under control. Keep the movement free of swinging or kicking.

Sets, repetitions, resistance, and rest follow the training plan. Establish a repeatable movement with a light load first; add resistance gradually after completing the planned repetitions with consistent control.
Use an assisted pull-up machine or another controlled assistance method when needed for the intended range. Reduce the added load or increase assistance if the movement becomes a swing.

Practice moving the arms out and back at the shoulder to train the rear deltoids.
Day 7 at 3:36 in Person/Andrew Huberman/Book/26/Protocols/YouTube/26/09/Day 7 - Shoulders and Arms

For the bent-over dumbbell version, stand a little wider than shoulder width and hinge forward with a dumbbell in each hand. A rear delt fly machine or a cable stack works too; face inward toward the machine.
With the elbows bent and fixed, raise the arms out and back so only the shoulders move. Keep the sternum high and the chin in, squeeze, then lower under control.

Huberman takes work sets to failure and adds load over time. Sets, repetitions, resistance, and rest follow the training plan. Establish a repeatable movement with a light load first; add resistance gradually after completing the planned repetitions with consistent control.

Keep continuous tension; letting the weights clank at the bottom means the lowering phase is uncontrolled. Back training reaches the rear deltoids only indirectly, so this isolation work fills the gap.
Demonstration: Huberman's rear delt fly, 3:20. Full notes: Person/Andrew Huberman/Book/26/Protocols/YouTube/26/09/Day 7 - Shoulders and Arms.
Practice a single-leg emphasis squat with the rear foot supported, developing leg strength and balance.
Day 2 at 3:42 in Person/Andrew Huberman/Book/26/Protocols/YouTube/26/09/Day 2 - Major Lower Body Muscles
Place the top of one foot on a stable low bench behind you and the other foot firmly on the floor. Begin without dumbbells, using light hand support for balance if needed.

Bend the front knee and hip to lower under control, then push through the front foot to stand. Find a stance in which the front heel stays down and the knee follows the toes. Keep the pelvis facing forward.

Sets, repetitions, resistance, and rest follow the training plan. Establish a repeatable movement with a light load first; add resistance gradually after completing the planned repetitions with consistent control.

Lower the support or use a regular split squat with the rear foot on the floor if balance or hip position limits the movement. Add dumbbells only after both sides feel controlled; stance changes should follow comfort and the intended movement rather than a fixed distance from the bench.
Demonstration: Huberman's split squat, 2:52. Full notes: Person/Andrew Huberman/Book/26/Protocols/YouTube/26/09/Day 2 - Major Lower Body Muscles.
Practice an overhand-grip elbow curl that trains the brachioradialis on the top of the forearm.
Stand holding a barbell or EZ bar with an overhand grip about shoulder width apart, arms hanging straight and elbows at your sides.
Bend the elbows to curl the bar up toward the shoulders without letting the elbows drift forward, then lower it under control.
Sets, repetitions, resistance, and rest follow the training plan. In the video it pairs with the Exercise/Body/Strength/Reverse Wrist Roll in a ladder taken to failure.
Keep the wrists straight and the bar in the palms; as you tire the bar tends to roll into the fingers. Use a lighter bar than for a Exercise/Body/Strength/Biceps Curl.
